{"schema":"o015-modular-backend-record","schema_version":"1.0.0","entity_type":"correction","id":"correction.o015-hab-adv-0075","recorded_at":"2026-08-22T08:15:00Z","responsible_workflow":"o015-habring-ch07-backend-v1","status":"applied","source_event_id":"O015-HAB-ADV-0075","source_edition_id":"edition.habring.convex-optimization.arxiv-2607-11664v1","affected_unit_ids":["unit.habring.v1.ch07"],"affected_segment_ids":["d90.hab.v1.ch07.seg0002","d90.hab.v1.ch07.seg0003"],"source_path":"authority/habring/source-v1/duality.tex","source_line_start":60,"source_line_end":140,"source_locator":"authority/habring/source-v1/duality.tex:60-140","surface":"Biconjugation and empty-family Gamma notation under proper-input conjugation","source_issue":"After restricting conjugation to proper inputs with codomain (-infinity,+infinity], a proper nonconvex f can still have f* identically plus infinity, so (f*)* is outside the stated convention; likewise, identifying an empty-family minorant supremum with f** would require that invalid second conjugation.","target_action":"Required both f and f* to be proper when introducing biconjugation and in the inequality f**<=f, noting the preceding convex case that guarantees properness; restricted the displayed Gamma equality to a nonempty proper-minorant family; and, for an empty family, defined only the right-hand supremum as identically minus infinity without denoting it f**.","correction_class":"determined_convention_consistency_correction","disposition":"applied","upstream_report_disposition":"not_submitted","evidence_artifact_id":"artifact.o015.adverse-ledger"}

{"schema":"o015-modular-backend-record","schema_version":"1.0.0","entity_type":"correction","id":"correction.o015-hab-adv-0086","recorded_at":"2026-08-22T16:45:00Z","responsible_workflow":"o015-habring-ch09-backend-v1","status":"applied","source_event_id":"O015-HAB-ADV-0086","source_edition_id":"edition.habring.convex-optimization.arxiv-2607-11664v1","affected_unit_ids":["unit.habring.v1.ch09"],"affected_segment_ids":["d90.hab.v1.ch09.seg0003"],"source_path":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex","source_line_start":87,"source_line_end":92,"source_locator":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex:87-92","surface":"Monge objective and feasibility","source_issue":"The source writes a minimum over all maps while omitting measurability from the optimization domain and without hypotheses ensuring that a feasible map or a minimizer exists.","target_action":"Made the definition self-contained with a bounded-below measurable cost and used the infimum over measurable feasible maps, explicitly adopting inf emptyset = +infinity.","correction_class":"determined_attainment_and_feasibility_correction","disposition":"applied","upstream_report_disposition":"not_submitted","evidence_artifact_id":"artifact.o015.adverse-ledger"}

{"schema":"o015-modular-backend-record","schema_version":"1.0.0","entity_type":"correction","id":"correction.o015-hab-adv-0087","recorded_at":"2026-08-22T16:45:00Z","responsible_workflow":"o015-habring-ch09-backend-v1","status":"applied","source_event_id":"O015-HAB-ADV-0087","source_edition_id":"edition.habring.convex-optimization.arxiv-2607-11664v1","affected_unit_ids":["unit.habring.v1.ch09"],"affected_segment_ids":["d90.hab.v1.ch09.seg0003"],"source_path":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex","source_line_start":94,"source_line_end":94,"source_locator":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex:94-94","surface":"Atomless target example for Monge infeasibility","source_issue":"The source invokes absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure without placing Y in Euclidean space, and its footnote identifies absolute continuity with having no point masses although atomlessness is only a consequence, not an equivalent definition.","target_action":"Specified Y as a subset of Euclidean space in this example and stated that absolute continuity in particular implies absence of point masses.","correction_class":"determined_domain_and_implication_correction","disposition":"applied","upstream_report_disposition":"not_submitted","evidence_artifact_id":"artifact.o015.adverse-ledger"}

{"schema":"o015-modular-backend-record","schema_version":"1.0.0","entity_type":"correction","id":"correction.o015-hab-adv-0088","recorded_at":"2026-08-22T16:45:00Z","responsible_workflow":"o015-habring-ch09-backend-v1","status":"applied","source_event_id":"O015-HAB-ADV-0088","source_edition_id":"edition.habring.convex-optimization.arxiv-2607-11664v1","affected_unit_ids":["unit.habring.v1.ch09"],"affected_segment_ids":["d90.hab.v1.ch09.seg0004"],"source_path":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex","source_line_start":112,"source_line_end":118,"source_locator":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex:112-118","surface":"Existence of a Kantorovich optimizer","source_issue":"The theorem asserts existence for unspecified X and Y, while its proof assumes weak compactness of the coupling set merely because couplings are probability measures; probability measures are not weakly compact on arbitrary measurable or topological spaces.","target_action":"Required Polish spaces with their Borel sigma-algebras and rewrote the sketch using tight fixed marginals, Prokhorov compactness, weak closedness of the coupling set, and lower semicontinuity for a bounded-below lsc cost.","correction_class":"determined_topological_hypothesis_and_proof_correction","disposition":"applied","upstream_report_disposition":"not_submitted","evidence_artifact_id":"artifact.o015.adverse-ledger"}

{"schema":"o015-modular-backend-record","schema_version":"1.0.0","entity_type":"correction","id":"correction.o015-hab-adv-0089","recorded_at":"2026-08-22T16:45:00Z","responsible_workflow":"o015-habring-ch09-backend-v1","status":"applied","source_event_id":"O015-HAB-ADV-0089","source_edition_id":"edition.habring.convex-optimization.arxiv-2607-11664v1","affected_unit_ids":["unit.habring.v1.ch09"],"affected_segment_ids":["d90.hab.v1.ch09.seg0004"],"source_path":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex","source_line_start":122,"source_line_end":129,"source_locator":"authority/habring/source-v1/optimal_transport.tex:122-129","surface":"Wasserstein-p definition and metric claim","source_issue":"The source uses a norm without specifying a normed space and ends with the incomplete phrase 'finite p-th', while W_p is finite and a metric only on probability measures with finite p-th moment under an appropriate metric-space scope.","target_action":"Used a Polish metric space (X,d), defined P_p(X) by a finite p-th moment, used the cost d(x,y)^p, and restricted the metric claim to P_p(X).","correction_class":"determined_metric_space_and_moment_scope_correction","disposition":"applied","upstream_report_disposition":"not_submitted","evidence_artifact_id":"artifact.o015.adverse-ledger"}
